A2_Scope.description: This chapter defines the axiomatic and operational structure of the Behavioral Change Journey (BCJ) in BCM 2.0. It describes all phases of behavioral change, the underlying transition conditions, and the coupling with awareness, willingness, utility, and segment logic. The module is mandatory for all simulations, models, and interventions that represent behavioral change phase trajectories.

goals: Realistic, formally representable description and analysis of behavioral change over time
Explicit linkage with awareness, utility functions, and segments
Foundation for agent-based simulations and evidence-based intervention architecture
Ensuring traceability and measurability of phases and transitions

A4_Axioms.title: Phased Nature of Behavioral Change
A4_Axioms.description: Behavioral change does not occur discretely, but through five sequential phases representing different psychological states.
A4_Axioms.formula: BCJ = { PreC, Cont, Prep, Act, Main }

A4_Axioms.title: Phase Transitions Are Probabilistic
A4_Axioms.description: Transitions between phases are not deterministic but modeled via transition probabilities.
A4_Axioms.formula: P_{i→j}(t) = f(W(t), A_mod(t), S(t), B(t), C(t))

A4_Axioms.title: Awareness as Entry Condition
A4_Axioms.description: A transition from Pre-Contemplation to Contemplation is only possible if situational awareness is activated.

A4_Axioms.title: Willingness Dominates Preparation and Action
A4_Axioms.description: Without sufficient willingness, transitions to Preparation or Action are not possible.

A4_Axioms.title: Stabilization via Habit and Reinforcement
A4_Axioms.description: The transition to Maintenance depends on social reinforcement and habit formation.

A4_Axioms.title: Systemic Possibility of Relapse
A4_Axioms.description: All phases may regress to earlier phases due to contextual changes, negative experiences, or norm violations.

A4_Axioms.title: Segment-Dependent Phase Duration
A4_Axioms.description: Phase duration and transition intensity vary by behavioral change segment.

A4_Axioms.title: Phases Modulate Utility Functions
A4_Axioms.description: Each phase modulates the weighting of the three utility functions.
A4_Axioms.formula: N(t) = ω_ind,i * N_ind(t) + ω_kol,i * N_kol(t) + ω_id,i * N_id(t)

A4_Axioms.title: BCJ Is Complementary to Willingness
A4_Axioms.description: The Behavioral Change Journey is not a consequence of willingness but feeds back into it.

A4_Axioms.title: The Journey Is Experimentally Measurable
A4_Axioms.description: Phases can be identified via observable indicators such as awareness levels, search behavior, intention, and repetition.

requirements: Loaded modules for Awareness, Willingness, Utility, and Segment Logic
Defined context vector for each application

integration: Direct coupling to Awareness, Willingness, Utility, and Segment modules
Compatible with all agent-based simulation architectures in BCM

conditions: All mandatory modules must be integrated
Commercial and scientific use requires written permission from FehrAdvice & Partners AG

summary: Realistic modeling of behavioral change over time
Direct coupling with awareness, willingness, utility, and segment logic
Applicable to simulation, intervention, and policy design
